title: Sunny Hears the Rain | Bedtime Story
description: When rain begins to fall in the Australian bush, Sunny the little quokka finds shelter under a large fern leaf and listens to the rain make different sounds all around her. A peaceful rain lullaby story from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
The bush had been very warm all afternoon, and now, as the sun dipped below the trees, something new came drifting in on the air. Something cool. Something quiet. And then the first drop fell.

Pitter. Then another. Pitter-pat.

Sunny the little quokka looked up at the sky with her soft round eyes. The rain was coming. She took a few quick steps along the bush path and found — just in time — a big, beautiful fern. Its frond curled out over the ground like a green umbrella, wide enough and low enough for a small quokka to sit right underneath.

Sunny tucked herself in and listened.

On the leaves above her, the rain went tap-tap-tap, light and quick, like tiny dancing feet. On the broad flat rock nearby, it went drum-drum-drum, steady and low. And from the edge of the big banksia tree, the water gathered itself into drops and fell — drip... drip... drip — slow and round and deliberate, like a clock measuring out the night.

Sunny closed her eyes. She could hear all the sounds at once now — the tapping and the drumming and the dripping — and together they made something that felt a great deal like music. Like a song the rain had always known.

She pulled her little paws close to her chest. The air smelled of wet earth and green leaves and something sweet she couldn't quite name. Her breathing grew slow. The rain kept playing its quiet song.

And Sunny slept.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, rain. Goodnight, little one.
